mappings.rationale: The task asks for the decimal classification of an irrational square root.
mappings.answerReason: If √2 were a reduced fraction p/q, then p²=2q² would force both p and q to be even. Thus √2 is irrational and its decimal expansion neither terminates nor repeats.

mappings.rationale: Guaranteed divisibility by 12 requires a factor of 3 and at least two factors of 2. These can be established through factoring or residue cases.
mappings.answerReason: Write the expression as n²(n-1)(n+1). One of the three consecutive integers is divisible by 3. If n is even, 4 divides n²; if n is odd, both neighbors are even. For n=2 the expression is 12, so divisibility by 24 is not guaranteed.

mappings.rationale: Equal rhombus sides and circle radii produce two equilateral triangles, whose areas determine the rhombus area.
mappings.answerReason: Let O be the circle center and P the opposite rhombus vertex. OP is a radius of length 16, so the diagonal OP splits the rhombus into two equilateral triangles of side 16. Their total area is 2(16²√3/4)=128√3.

mappings.rationale: The arithmetic-series sum gives an integer equation K(K+1)=2N². A finite bound or coprime-factor restrictions allows complete checking.
mappings.answerReason: For 1≤N≤99, K(K+1)/2≤9801 gives K≤139. Coprimality of K and K+1 reduces the search to K=u², K+1=2v² or K=2u², K+1=v². Checking these bounded possibilities gives K=1,8,49, with N=1,6,35.
limitations: N is interpreted as the nonnegative integer square root. Allowing arbitrary negative N would make N<100 ineffective as an upper bound.

mappings.rationale: The map scale converts the short diagonal to an actual length. The 60-degree rhombus then gives equilateral-triangle and area relationships.
mappings.answerReason: The actual short diagonal is (3/16)(400/(3/2))=50 miles. A rhombus diagonal opposite a 60-degree angle equals its side, so its area is 2(50²√3/4)=1250√3.

mappings.rationale: The altitude relates the legs and hypotenuse through equal-area formulas or similar right triangles, leading to the reciprocal-square identity.
mappings.answerReason: Equating areas gives ab=cx. Therefore 1/x²=c²/(a²b²)=(a²+b²)/(a²b²)=1/a²+1/b².

mappings.rationale: The unknown leg square is a difference of squares, and consecutive hypotenuse and leg lengths differ by one.
mappings.answerReason: The second leg satisfies b²=c²-a²=(c-a)(c+a). Since c>a and they are consecutive integers, c-a=1, giving b²=c+a.

mappings.rationale: Substituting gt=V-V₀ and factoring out t transforms the formulas into an equality that can be rearranged for t.

limitations: The displayed expression requires V+V₀≠0. When V+V₀=0, the elimination gives S=0 rather than this quotient.
